sections.name: INSTRUCTIONS FOR ATTORNEYS COMPLETING CIVIL COVER SHEET FORM JS 44
sentences: Authority For Civil Cover Sheet The JS 44 civil cover sheet and the information contained herein neither replaces nor supplements the filings and service of pleading or other papers as required by law, except as provided by local rules of court.
This form, approved by the Judicial Conference of the United States in September 1974, is required for the use of the Clerk of Court for the purpose of initiating the civil docket sheet.
Consequently, a civil cover sheet is submitted to the Clerk of Court for each civil complaint filed.
The attorney filing a case should complete the form as follows: (a) Plaintiffs-Defendants.
Enter names (last, first, middle initial) of plaintiff and defendant.
If the plaintiff or defendant is a government agency, use only the full name or standard abbreviations.
If the plaintiff or defendant is an official within a government agency, identify first the agency and then the official, giving both name and title. (b) County of Residence.
For each civil case filed, except U.S. plaintiff cases, enter the name of the county where the first listed plaintiff resides at the time of filing.

In U.S. plaintiff cases, enter the name of the county in which the first listed defendant resides at the time of filing. (NOTE: In land condemnation cases, the county of residence of the "defendant" is the location of the tract of land involved.) (c) Attorneys.
Enter the firm name, address, telephone number, and attorney of record.
If there are several attorneys, list them on an attachment, noting in this section "(see attachment)".
II. Jurisdiction.
The basis of jurisdiction is set forth under Rule 8(a), F.R.Cv.P., which requires that jurisdictions be shown in pleadings.
Place an "X" in one of the boxes.
If there is more than one basis of jurisdiction, precedence is given in the order shown below.
United States plaintiff. (1) Jurisdiction based on 28 U.S.C. 1345 and 1348.
Suits by agencies and officers of the United States are included here.

United States defendant. (2) When the plaintiff is suing the United States, its officers or agencies, place an "X" in this box. Federal question. (3) This refers to suits under 28 U.S.C. 1331, where jurisdiction arises under the Constitution of the United States, an amendment to the Constitution, an act of Congress or a treaty of the United States.
In cases where the U.S. is a party, the U.S. plaintiff or defendant code takes precedence, and box 1 or 2 should be marked.
Diversity of citizenship. (4) This refers to suits under 28 U.S.C. 1332, where parties are citizens of different states.

When Box 4 is checked, the citizenship of the different parties must be checked. (See Section III below; NOTE: federal question actions take precedence over diversity cases.) III. Residence (citizenship) of Principal Parties.
This section of the JS 44 is to be completed if diversity of citizenship was indicated above.
Mark this section for each principal party.
IV. Nature of Suit.
Place an "X" in the appropriate box. If there are multiple nature of suit codes associated with the case, pick the nature of suit code that is most applicable.
Click here for: Nature of Suit Code Descriptions.
Place an "X" in one of the seven boxes.
Original Proceedings. (1) Cases which originate in the United States district courts.
Removed from State Court. (2) Proceedings initiated in state courts may be removed to the district courts under Title 28 U.S.C., Section 1441.
Remanded from Appellate Court. (3) Check this box for cases remanded to the district court for further action.
Use the date of remand as the filing date.
Reinstated or Reopened. (4) Check this box for cases reinstated or reopened in the district court.
Use the reopening date as the filing date.
Transferred from Another District. (5) For cases transferred under Title 28 U.S.C. Section 1404(a).
Do not use this for within district transfers or multidistrict litigation transfers.
Multidistrict Litigation – Transfer. (6) Check this box when a multidistrict case is transferred into the district under authority of Title 28 U.S.C. Section 1407.
Multidistrict Litigation – Direct File. (8) Check this box when a multidistrict case is filed in the same district as the Master MDL docket.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THERE IS NOT AN ORIGIN CODE 7. Origin Code 7 was used for historical records and is no longer relevant due to changes in statute.
VI. Cause of Action.
Report the civil statute directly related to the cause of action and give a brief description of the cause.
Do not cite jurisdictional statutes unless diversity.
Example: U.S. Civil Statute: 47 USC 553 Brief Description: Unauthorized reception of cable service.
VII. Requested in Complaint.
Place an "X" in this box if you are filing a class action under Rule 23, F.R.Cv.P.
In this space enter the actual dollar amount being demanded or indicate other demand, such as a preliminary injunction.
Check the appropriate box to indicate whether or not a jury is being demanded.
This section of the JS 44 is used to reference related pending cases, if any. If there are related pending cases, insert the docket numbers and the corresponding judge names for such cases.
Date and Attorney Signature.
Date and sign the civil cover sheet.

sections.name: COMPLAINT AND JURY DEMAND
sentences: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT: This is an action for an award of damages, attorneys’ fees, and other relief on behalf of the Plaintiff, Theresa Reed (“Plaintiff”), a former employee of Defendant, Old Village Master Painters Ltd. (“Defendant Old Village), owned and operated by Defendant, Edwin Hutter Stulb IV (“Stulb”), who has been harmed by the Defendants’ discriminatory and retaliatory employment practices.

This action is brought under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. §2000(e), et seq., as amended by the Civil Rights Act of 1991 (“Title VII”), the Americans with Disabilities Act, 42 U.S.C. §12101, et seq. (“ADA”), and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. §951 et seq. (“PHRA”).

sections.name: JURISDICTION AND VENUE:
sentences: The jurisdiction of this Court is invoked, and venue is proper in this district, pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§1331 and 1391, as Plaintiff’s claims are substantively based on Title VII and the ADA. The supplemental jurisdiction of this Court is invoked pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1367 to consider Plaintiff’s claims arising under the PHRA.
All conditions precedent to the institution of this suit have been fulfilled and Plaintiff has satisfied all other jurisdictional prerequisites to the maintenance of this action.
On August 28, 2025, a Notice of Right to Sue was issued by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and this action has been filed within ninety (90) days of receipt of said notice.

sections.name: PARTIES:
sentences: Plaintiff, Theresa Reed (“Plaintiff”), is an adult individual and citizen of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, residing therein at 1245 Fieldstone Court, Quakertown, Pennsylvania 18951.

Defendant, Old Village Master Painters Ltd. (“Defendant Old Village”), is a business organized and existing under the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, maintaining an office therein at 1048 Gypsy Hill Road, Gwynedd Valley, Pennsylvania 19437.
Defendant, Edwin Hutter Stulb IV (“Stulb”), is an adult individual and citizen of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, residing therein at 1048 Gypsy Hill Road, Gwynedd Valley, Pennsylvania 19437.

At all times relevant hereto, Defendant Old Village was acting through its agents, servants, and employees, including Stulb, who were acting within the scope of their authority, course of employment, and under the direct control of the Defendant.

sections.name: STATEMENT OF FACTS:
sentences: Plaintiff was employed by Defendant Old Village from on or about August 25, 2020 until September 16, 2022, the date of her termination.
Upon commencing employment with Defendant Old Village, Plaintiff held the position of Painter.
Thereafter, Defendants promoted Plaintiff to the role of Administrative Assistant.
At all times relevant hereto, Plaintiff maintained a satisfactory job performance.
At no time during Plaintiff’s employment did Defendants provide her with training on any alleged harassment or discrimination policies.
Nor did Defendants provide Plaintiff with an understanding of what steps to take if she felt harassed at work.
In her role as Administrative Assistant, Plaintiff reported directly to Defendant Edwin Hutter Stulb IV (“Stulb”), Owner.

Throughout Plaintiff’s employment, Defendant Old Village, through its agents, servants, and employees, including, but not limited to, Stulb, subjected her to a hostile work environment through various instances of severe and pervasive sexual harassment.

By way of example, on August 27, 2021, Stulb sent Plaintiff several text messages stating that he might retire or die, and repeatedly asked Plaintiff if the aforementioned messages upset her. Thereafter, on September 8, 2021, Stulb inquired as to whether Plaintiff informed her husband about his text messages by texting her “[a]re our conversations strictly between you and me?” Additionally, on September 23, 2021, Stulb sent Plaintiff a text message complimenting a photo that he saw of Plaintiff.

Acknowledging the sexual nature of his text messages to Plaintiff, on October 10, 2021, Stulb texted Plaintiff that if she and her husband are “still close”, he felt embarrassed about “the things [he] had said” to her. On October 22, 2021, Stulb texted Plaintiff that it was her voice that got the Defendants an appointment with a client.

As further sexual harassment, on November 22, 2021, Stulb texted Plaintiff that if he were younger and Plaintiff were single, he would ask Plaintiff to marry him. In response, Plaintiff deflected his sexual advances by continuing to ask Stulb about the unpaid wages he owed her. On December 21, 2021, Stulb texted Plaintiff that she is the “one bright spot that keeps [him] moving forward,” to which Plaintiff did not respond.
On April 26, 2022, Stulb texted Plaintiff that he “need[ed] and want[ed]” Plaintiff.
Again, Plaintiff refused to respond to Stulb’s sexually harassing messages.
As further harassment, on June 17, 2022, Stulb asked Plaintiff whether she and her daughter would move in with him, to which Plaintiff refused to respond.
Over the next two days, Stulb proceeded to send Plaintiff numerous text messages demanding that Plaintiff speak with him regarding his request and for Plaintiff to respond to his messages.
Plaintiff continued to evade Stulb’s sexual advances by ignoring his text messages.
In connection thereto, on June 20, 2022, Stulb asked Plaintiff whether his text messages had upset Plaintiff’s husband.
On July 2, 2022, Stulb invited Plaintiff to have lunch with him that following Tuesday.

In rejection of his advances, Plaintiff replied that she was unavailable that day. Again acknowledging the sexual nature of his text messages, on July 4, 2022, Stulb asked Plaintiff whether his messages had upset her husband.
On July 6, 2022, Stulb asked Plaintiff to have lunch with him on Friday because he wanted to speak to her in person.

In rejection of Stulb’s ongoing advances, Plaintiff ignored his invitation to have lunch with him. On July 26, 2022, Plaintiff was hospitalized after suffering an Ischemic Stroke caused by a blood clot.

Said medical condition constitutes a disability within the meanings of the Americans with Disabilities Act (“ADA”) and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act (“PHRA”) in that it substantially impairs one or more of Plaintiff’s major life activities, including, but not limited to, speaking, walking, standing, and writing.
The next day, Plaintiff’s husband, Jeff Reed (“Reed”), requested a reasonable accommodation on Plaintiff’s behalf.
Reed informed Stulb about Plaintiff’s condition and asked whether she could take a medical leave of absence due to the fact that she was unable to return to work at that time.
In response thereto, Stulb approved Plaintiff’s request for a medical leave of absence while Plaintiff recovered from her stroke.
Shortly thereafter, on or about August 3, 2022, Stulb replaced Plaintiff with another Administrative Assistant who did not suffer from a disability, Nancy (last name unknown) (“Nancy”).
On August 6, 2022, Plaintiff was discharged from the hospital.
Shortly thereafter, Plaintiff began physical therapy, speech therapy, and occupational rehabilitation.
On or about August 16, 2022, Plaintiff’s Occupational Therapist, Michelle Foley (“Foley”), informed her that she could return to work so long as she was not required to drive.
Since Plaintiff performed her work as an Administrative Assistant from home, her position did not require her to drive.

Accordingly, Plaintiff was able to return to her position at Defendant Old Village and perform the essential functions of her job. In connection thereto, on or about August 24, 2022, Plaintiff reached out to Stulb to inform him that she could return to work.
However, Stulb avoided Plaintiff’s numerous calls and text messages.

As further disability discrimination and in retaliation for requesting a reasonable accommodation, on or about September 1, 2022, Stulb rejected Plaintiff’s requests to return to her position at Defendant Old Village.
On September 16, 2022, Stulb again rejected Plaintiff’s request to return to her position at Defendant Old Village.
Accordingly, effective September 16, 2022, Defendants terminated Plaintiff’s employment due to her disability and/or in retaliation for requesting a reasonable accommodation for her disability.

On February 1, 2023, Plaintiff filed a charge of discrimination against the Defendants with the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (“PHRC”) that was dual filed with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”).
On or about February 8, 2023, Stulb informed the law firm of Plaintiff’s counsel, The Gold Law Firm, P.C., that he was in receipt of Plaintiff’s charge of discrimination.

In clear retaliation against Plaintiff for filing a charge of discrimination, Stulb proceeded to threaten that if The Gold Law Firm, P.C. failed to notify Stulb that Plaintiff’s claims of discrimination “have been cancelled” that he would pursue false criminal claims against Plaintiff and her husband with the local police station.

Curiously, although Stulb’s false criminal allegations concerned conduct that Plaintiff allegedly committed over a year ago, Stulb admitted that he waited to pursue said allegations “in anticipation of the issues with [Plaintiff] being addressed.” On or about February 9, 2023, Stulb reached out to The Gold Law Firm, P.C. demanding to receive documentation proving that Plaintiff’s claims of discrimination were dismissed by February 16, 2023, or he would pursue “all the avenues” against Plaintiff and her husband.
On or about February 15, 2023, Stulb again reached out to The Gold Law Firm, C. asking whether the firm still represented Plaintiff.

Stulb then threatened that if the firm failed to respond to him, he would pursue his false criminal claims against Plaintiff and her husband later that day Stulb aided, abetted, incited, compelled and/or coerced the unlawful acts of sexual harassment, disability discrimination and retaliation alleged herein including the termination of Plaintiff’s employment.

sections.name: COUNT I
sentences: (Title VII – Sex Discrimination, Sexual Harassment, Hostile Work Environment, Retaliation) Plaintiff v. Defendants Plaintiff incorporates by reference paragraphs 1 through 42 of this Complaint as though fully set forth at length herein.

The actions of Defendant Old Village, through its agents, servants, and employees, including, but not limited to, Defendant Stulb, in subjecting Plaintiff to discrimination based on her sex, a hostile work environment through various instances of sexual harassment, and retaliation for opposing and rejecting sexual harassment in the workplace, constituted violations of Title VII. As a direct result of the aforesaid unlawful discriminatory and retaliatory employment practices engaged in by the Defendants in violation of Title VII, Plaintiff has sustained permanent and irreparable harm, resulting in the termination of her employment, which caused her to sustain a loss of earnings, plus the value of certain benefits, plus loss of future earning power, plus back pay, front pay, and interest due thereon.

As further direct result of the aforesaid unlawful discriminatory and retaliatory employment practices engaged in by the Defendants in violation of Title VII, Plaintiff suffered severe emotional distress, embarrassment, humiliation, and loss of self-esteem.

sections.name: COUNT II
sentences: (ADA – Disability Discrimination, Retaliation) Plaintiff v. Defendants Plaintiff incorporates by reference paragraphs 1 through 46 of this Complaint as though fully set forth at length herein.

The actions of Defendant Old Village, through its agents, servants, and employees, including, but not limited to, Defendant Stulb, in subjecting Plaintiff to discrimination based on her disability, and in retaliating against Plaintiff for requesting a reasonable accommodation for her disability, constituted violations of the ADA. As a direct result of the aforesaid unlawful discriminatory and retaliatory employment practices engaged in by the Defendants in violation of the ADA, Plaintiff sustained permanent and irreparable harm, resulting in the termination of her employment, which caused her to sustain a loss of earnings, plus the value of certain benefits, plus loss of future earning power, plus back pay, and front pay and interest due thereon.

As a further direct result of the aforesaid unlawful discriminatory and retaliatory employment practices engaged in by the Defendants in violation of the ADA, Plaintiff suffered severe emotional distress, embarrassment, humiliation, and loss of self-esteem.

sections.name: COUNT III
sentences: (PHRA – Sex Discrimination, Sexual Harassment, Hostile Work Environment, Disability Discrimination, Retaliation) Plaintiff v. Defendants Plaintiff incorporates by reference paragraphs 1 through 50 of this Complaint as though fully set forth at length herein.

The actions of Defendant Old Village, through its agents, servants, and employees, including, but not limited to, Defendant Stulb, in subjecting Plaintiff to discrimination based on her sex and disability, a hostile work environment through various instances of sexual harassment, and retaliation for requesting a reasonable accommodation for her disability and opposing and rejecting sexual harassment in the workplace, constituted violations of the PHRA.

As a direct result of the aforesaid unlawful discriminatory and retaliatory employment practices engaged in by the Defendants in violation of the PHRA, Plaintiff has sustained permanent and irreparable harm, resulting in the termination of her employment, which caused her to sustain a loss of earnings, plus the value of certain benefits, plus loss of future earning power, plus back pay, front pay, and interest due thereon.

As further direct result of the aforesaid unlawful discriminatory and retaliatory employment practices engaged in by the Defendants in violation of the PHRA, Plaintiff suffered severe emotional distress, embarrassment, humiliation, and loss of self-esteem.

sections.name: PRAYER FOR RELIEF
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates by reference paragraphs 1 through 54 of this Complaint as though fully set forth at length herein.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests that this Court enter judgment in her favor and against the Defendants, and order that: a. Defendants compensate Plaintiff with a rate of pay and other benefits and emoluments of employment to which she would have been entitled had she not been subjected to unlawful discrimination and retaliation; b. Defendants compensate Plaintiff with an award of front pay, if appropriate; c. Defendants pay to Plaintiff punitive damages, compensatory damages for future pecuniary losses, pain, suffering, inconvenience, mental anguish, loss of enjoyment of life and other nonpecuniary losses as allowable; d. Defendants pay to Plaintiff pre- and post-judgment interest, costs of suit and attorney and expert witness fees as allowed by law; e. The Court award such other relief as is deemed just and proper.
